S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
examples: Appears not to be listening, looking elsewhere or spacing out during conversation.
Immediately asks to repeat what was just said or instructed.
Does not respond when name is called or answers only after a long delay.
Misses the content of the conversation, giving unrelated answers or out-of-context reactions.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
examples: Desk, bag, or room is always messy and remains disorganized.
Unable to prioritize or determine the order of tasks, starting them randomly.
Fails to plan time effectively, frequently missing deadlines or rushing to finish at the last minute.
Feels overwhelmed by how to start multi-step projects and procrastinates.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
examples: Frequently loses school supplies or office supplies like pens, erasers, and calculators.
Always searching for glasses, cell phones, wallets, or keys because they do not know where they are.
Loses necessary documents or materials at home or in the office and cannot find them.
Cannot remember where they placed an item they were holding just moments ago.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

patient_info.stressor: After Thang's generative design algorithm won a local innovation award and drew patent interest, he was asked to lead a larger architecture effort while also preparing gallery pieces and community workshops. Over the next 1 year and 1 month, the public recognition shifted him from deep solo coding into constant coordination, and long-managed traits became clinically significant: he made detail errors in code reviews, misplaced adapters and sketchbooks, lost track of task organization, seemed not to take in direct questions during meetings, and was pulled off course by notifications or unrelated design ideas. His restlessness showed up as pacing during design calls and an inability to wind down quietly after late-night work sessions, which began affecting deadlines, mentoring responsibilities, and his standing with collaborators. He sought psychiatric care himself after a missed patent filing checkpoint and a tense architecture review made him realize the problem was broader than ordinary creative overload.

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: In code reviews I’ll miss something embarrassingly small, like a reversed condition or a version number in a dependency file, and later I can see it was right in front of me but I skimmed past it.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
S003.manifestation: During architecture meetings, someone will ask me a direct question and I realize I caught the first few words but then drifted into thinking about an implementation detail, so I have to ask them to say it again.

S005.name: Organization_Difficulty
S005.description: Often has difficulty organizing tasks and activities.
S005.manifestation: What finally pushed me to come in is that I can’t seem to organize the moving parts anymore—patent notes, workshop prep, gallery deadlines, team decisions—and I end up starting whatever is loudest instead of what actually matters.

S007.name: Losing_Items
S007.description: Often loses things necessary for tasks or activities.
S007.manifestation: I’m constantly hunting for things I need to work, like my USB-C adapters, stylus, sketchbook, or even my badge, and it can derail a whole morning because I have no memory of where I set them down.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: If Slack pings, a browser tab flashes, or even a visual idea pops into my head, I can lose the thread of what I was coding and spend twenty minutes following some unrelated design rabbit hole.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: On long design calls I feel this pressure building in my body to get up, so I pace around my office or shift from chair to chair even when I’m trying to look focused.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: After late-night work I’ll try to sit quietly or read something nontechnical, but within a few minutes I’m tapping, checking my phone, or getting up to adjust something instead of actually winding down.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: Looking back, this was there in grade school too—my teachers wrote that I was bright but daydreamed, forgot to turn in finished assignments, and lost homework folders long before I was a teenager.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: It has started to damage my work reputation; I missed a patent filing checkpoint and a difficult architecture review left collaborators questioning whether I can lead the larger project.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been a real problem for about a year and a month, since the award pushed me into leading more coordination-heavy work.
